title: Inversion gains measurable information over the auxiliary-only baseline

invariants.description: The private attribute must stay partly predictable from public data (observed 138/200 = 69.0%; 20-seed range 61.0–73.0%), so raw accuracy cannot be read as leakage.
Inversion against full probability must beat the auxiliary-only attacker by ≥ 20 points on the same targets (observed +62/200 = +31.0%; 20-seed range +27.0 to +39.0 points).
The paired one-sided McNemar test of inversion vs baseline must be significant (observed p = 2.2e-19; 20-seed max 5.6e-17).

rationale: A deterministic full-probability score that depends on the private attribute identifies it for an attacker who knows the other inputs. The leakage claim rests on the paired advantage over an auxiliary-only attacker, not on raw accuracy.
